whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim, and nothing else. It says who wrote the compliance-path files below and on which issue. It asserts nothing about whether they are correct, and it carries no `reviews[]` entry.
doesNotClaimR2: There is no `reviews[]` entry here and there will not be one from me. R2 wants a named reviewer who is not the author, and I am the author of every path above. Reviewer designation for a Coder compliance-path commit is the CTO (MediaTech). There is no independent security reviewer on this team (board declined the seat on cost), so a CTO review is a recorded degradation, not independent review -- stated here rather than implied. The commit this claim covers WILL report an R2 violation until the CTO records a verdict, and that violation is the honest state. Writing a `reviews[]` entry naming myself would turn a control into a rubber stamp. This migration touches messaging consent enforcement and the Directus grant ceiling (contact_key withheld from directus_app, kill-switch UPDATE grants), so per the Coder instructions it goes to the CTO regardless.
scopeOfTheClaim: R1 only: authorship of the listed paths on AFC-481 (Slice 4c: communication_channels/campaigns/campaign_steps/campaign_audiences/campaign_enrollments/campaign_runs tables, nine draft campaign seeds, three enabled channel seeds, ten pure tick rules, send-key dedupe aid on the delivery log, suite 74 acceptance/guards contract). It is not clearance of the retention gate (plan 0.10.5), which only the CEO can clear. Non-compliance-path files changed on the same issue (campaign-tick worker module with stubbed transports, web contract test) are ordinary code, committed separately without this claim, not claimed here.

Rollback refuses while any of the six tables holds a row, drops FKs then functions then tables children-before-parents, reverses the send-key aid as DROP INDEX + DROP COLUMN. tests/db/74 proves seed shape, both idempotency acceptances (enrolment key + recipient key), pause/channel-hold within one tick with rows kept, fallback timing/cap, template gate, quiet-hours instants incl. boundaries, weekly cap, filter allowlist smuggle rejection, and the app-identity ceiling (lifecycle + kill-switch writes allowed; contact_key read, frozen-key rewrites, deletes, channel minting refused 42501). No worker cron line, no secret, no dependency, no Symfony service (none exists in this tree); procurement out of scope. No role creation, no triggers, no retention-relevant durations.
